proof_attempt_summary: Two D-0.5 proposal versions developed the finite first-difference RM-CDF network, explicit rational primal witnesses, shortest-path/negative-cycle certificates, and a calibration-aware projection-inference route. The second version repaired the initial mathematical specification defects and documented exhaustive lawful attempts to obtain the closest comparator texts, but the Fan--Yu and Kim--Wooldridge theorem bodies remained inaccessible, so the same load-bearing field-novelty audit failed twice. A future retry should begin with those full texts, then apply the remaining overlap, final-period indexing, and bibliography repairs before asking for another field-tier review.
tldr: Can a multi-period relaxation of CDF parallel trends be analyzed jointly rather than cutoff by cutoff? The proposal asks whether finite-support first-difference relative-magnitude restrictions and CDF order form an exact network-potential model. It aims to prove negative-cycle compatibility, simultaneously attainable shortest-path CDF surfaces, sharp flow-dual bounds and distinct compatibility/conclusion frontiers, then propagate simultaneous observed-CDF bands through the model with pre-trend calibration uncertainty. The payoff is a distributionally coherent sensitivity analysis that can strictly reverse the sign of an ATT bound relative to thresholdwise analysis.
gap: Existing work separately establishes the causal importance of CDF parallel trends, relative-magnitude sensitivity for scalar event-study paths, distributional DiD identification under exact or dependence restrictions, and breakdown or simultaneous-band inference. No accessible theorem text inspected establishes the joint finite first-difference CDF-order network or its cross-period sharpness consequences; inaccessible Fan--Yu and Kim--Wooldridge theorem bodies limit the priority claim.
fill: Prove the network equivalence, simultaneous extremal surfaces, causal realizability, min-cost-flow and cycle certificates, a strict rational cross-period gain, and honest calibration-aware projection. Retain general second-difference smoothness only as an exact LP boundary case.
